items.definition:
relating to the thin tissue forming the outer layer of a body's surface
The skin is covered by epithelial tissue.

intensely painful; mentally agonizing
The pain in his leg was excruciating.

serving as a base or foundation
These foundational principles are essential for understanding the subject.

having one's true identity concealed
The celebrity traveled incognito to avoid the paparazzi.

not able to be destroyed
The superhero seemed to have an indestructible shield.

not harmful or offensive
The snake was innocuous, posing no threat to humans.

showing great skill or power
He gave a masterful performance on the piano.

the greatest possible
We aim for maximal efficiency in our operations.

combining or involving several academic disciplines or professional specializations
The project required a multidisciplinary approach.

pleasant to taste; acceptable or satisfactory
The food was not very palatable, but we ate it anyway.

affectedly and irritatingly grand, solemn, or self-important
His pompous attitude made him unpopular with his colleagues.

relating to or involving regeneration, especially of tissue or a lost part
Scientists are studying the regenerative properties of certain cells.

of or like a snake or serpent; winding and twisting like a snake.
The road followed a serpentine path up the mountain.

making a loud, confused noise; disorderly or noisy; excited, confused, or disorderly.
The crowd gave the band a tumultuous welcome.

forming a single or uniform entity.
The country operates under a unitary system of government.

relating to the Vedas or the period in which they were composed
Ancient Vedic texts describe early Indian philosophy.

having or showing a dislike or fear of people from other countries
His xenophobic comments caused a public outcry.

relating to confession, especially of sins or personal beliefs
She wrote a confessional poem about her struggles.

extremely complex and difficult to follow
The plot of the movie was so convoluted that I got lost.

having the opposite of the desired effect
Arguing with him would be counterproductive.

situated or occurring outside the cell
The extracellular matrix provides structural support to tissues.

relating to holography
The security feature on the banknote was holographic.

tending to stir up conflict; designed to cause fires
The politician's incendiary remarks sparked a heated debate.

relating to liturgy or public worship
The choir performed a beautiful liturgical chant.

relating to the branch of economics concerned with large-scale factors
The government is focused on macroeconomic stability.

having a limited or narrow outlook
Her views were criticized for being too parochial.

relating to the thorax (chest)
The patient suffered a thoracic injury.

designed to be useful or practical rather than attractive
The building had a very utilitarian design, focusing on function over aesthetics.

relating to or used in a vehicle
The accident caused significant vehicular damage.

hostile and aggressive
His belligerent attitude made it difficult to negotiate.

unlimited or immense
Her boundless energy allowed her to work tirelessly.

characterized by moral or cultural decline
The rich dessert was a truly decadent treat.

morally corrupt; wicked
The villain in the story was a truly depraved character.

having or displaying a passionate intensity
He was a fervent supporter of human rights.

relating to the study of family history
He spent years researching his genealogical tree.

extremely happy, peaceful, or picturesque
They spent an idyllic summer vacation in the countryside.

lacking power or ability; helpless
He felt completely impotent in the face of such overwhelming problems.

impossible to satisfy
He had an insatiable appetite for knowledge.

fearless; adventurous
The intrepid explorer ventured into the unknown jungle.

showing no mercy or pity
The merciless sun beat down on the desert.

having strong patriotic feelings
His nationalistic views were very strong.

annoyingly insensitive or slow to understand; (of an angle) greater than 90 degrees
He was too obtuse to understand the subtle hint.

relating to or in the form of minute separate particles
Air pollution often includes fine particulate matter.

tenacious (tending to keep a firm hold of something; not readily relinquishing a position, principle, or course of action; determined)
She was a tenacious negotiator, never giving up until she got the best deal.

relating to Athens, Greece
The Athenian philosophers made significant contributions to Western thought.

important; significant
The decision had consequential effects on the company's future.

departing from usual or accepted standards
His behavior was considered deviant by societal norms.

relating to the reign of Queen Elizabeth I of England
Shakespeare wrote many plays during the Elizabethan era.

bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind
The old photographs were evocative of a bygone era.

Continuing without interruption; constant.
The incessant rain made the roads slippery.

Too many to be counted; countless.
There are innumerable stars in the night sky.

Ignorant of or uninterested in cultures, ideas, or peoples outside one's own experience; narrow-minded.
The small community was quite insular, rarely interacting with outsiders.

Too great to be overcome.
The challenges seemed insurmountable at first.

relating to the system of methods used in a particular area of study or activity
The research paper had a strong methodological approach.

relating to the sense of smell
Dogs have a highly developed olfactory sense.

Representing the most perfect or typical example of a quality or class.
He was the quintessential New Yorker.

relating to zoology or animals
The zoological garden houses many rare species.

showing or feeling active opposition or hostility
Their relationship became increasingly antagonistic.

relating to the physics of the earth
The team conducted a geophysical survey of the area.

emitting light as a result of being heated
The old house still used incandescent light bulbs.

incapable of making mistakes or being wrong
Even experts are not infallible; they can make errors.

relating to the direct conversion of light into electricity
Photovoltaic cells are used to generate solar power.

having two or more different colors
The pied piper led the children away.

splendid and expensive-looking
They enjoyed a sumptuous feast at the palace.
